thread.label: Genesis 4:1-24
thread.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.

precepts.label: Genesis 3:21
precepts.why:
“Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.” That don't mean they were butt naked and needed clothes. It means God gave them a way to get forgiveness of their sin. Animal sacrifice was introduced right here, in Genesis 3:21: God clothed them with righteousness and forgiveness.

That is the key to Genesis 4. Cain “brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Abel “brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.” “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering”, because Abel's offering was in accordance with Genesis 3:21. Cain did not roll that way. He decided he was not going to do what God said and brought fruits and vegetables instead.

“But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance falling means he got mad. He got pissed off. God asked him, “Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?” and told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Doing well was obeying what God had set in place; sin lying at the door was disobedience.

So the difference between Cain and Abel was not the gift; it was obedience. Abel followed the way God had already shown his parents, and Cain replaced it with his own way. That disobedience is where Cain's line started.

precepts.label: Genesis 3:16
precepts.why:
God said to Cain, “And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” This is a parable. God is speaking about the spiritual demon, Satan: the “thee” is Satan, and it is Cain's desire that would be unto him.

To see the pattern, go back to Genesis 3:16. “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” If a woman desires anything, whether it is sex, wisdom, knowledge or money, it must be to her husband, and he rules over her.

Read Genesis 4:7 with that in mind. Just as a woman's desire is to her husband, Cain's desire would be to Satan. Anything Cain wanted, he would have to go to Satan for it, and Satan would rule over him.

So Satan was over Cain and over his seed. When we read about Cain's children, the city, the cattle, the music, the weapons and Lamech's vengeance, we should not read them as holy and righteous. This is Cain's seed, and their desire is always unto Satan.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 39:25-27
precepts.why:
After Abel was slain, “Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city”. If Cain was the only child left, why would he need to build a city? There were already thousands upon thousands of people on the earth. He named the city after his son Enoch, and down the line came Lamech, who took two wives, the first time multiple wives appear in scripture.

Adah bore Jabal, “the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.” What could be wrong with tents and cattle? Ecclesiasticus answers: “For the good are good things created from the beginning: so evil things for sinners.” From the beginning means from the time of Cain and Abel. “The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.” “All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.”

Bring it up to today. What do they do with food? GMOs, and things put inside the chicken and the cows to make them larger, and that causes sickness. They monopolize water and bottle it. With fire they create bombs, even nuclear fire. With iron they make bullets and guns to kill people. The milk today is not the same milk we drank as children. The clothing is made of mixed fabrics. Everything good, the sinful man turns to evil.

That is Cain's city. Jabal dealt in cattle with pricing and unrighteousness. His brother Jubal was “the father of all such as handle the harp and organ”, and it was not holy music: it was music about shake your ass, show me what you going with. Damn. It was songs about murder, drugs, debauchery and adultery, the same wicked songs many love today. Zillah bore Tubal-cain, “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”: that man was making all kinds of weapons. Good things created from the beginning, turned into evil by the seed whose desire was to Satan.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 27:2
precepts.why:
“As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so doth sin stick close between buying and selling.” When you are dealing in business with a sinner, the balances will be offset, because he always takes the favor, exceedingly. He will not take a five percent interest; he wants a hundred or two hundred percent.

That opens up Jabal, “the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.” It sounds harmless, but this is the seed of Cain in Cain's city. Jabal was dealing in tents and cattle with pricing and unrighteousness, buying and selling with sin stuck fast in between.

What Cain's seed did in the city of Enoch is what sinners do in business today. There is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:10-12
precepts.why:
In case anyone doubts that Satan ruled over Cain, John explains it: “In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.” There are children of God on the earth, and there are children of the devil.

John was correcting the Israelites he wrote to: “For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.” “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” He was telling them, do not be like Cain. And who is that wicked one? The devil of verse 10. Cain was under Satan; Satan was his father.

“And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” That is Genesis 4: Abel did well and was accepted, Cain did not do well, his desire went to Satan, and “Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.”

It shows in Cain's seed. Lamech said, “I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt.” “If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.” They did not just kill the one man who hurt Lamech; they wiped out that whole lineage: the sons, the daughters, the aunts, the grandparents. That is how Esau gets down too. Remember who their desire was to: Satan. Everybody comes from Adam, but not everybody is a child of God.

thread.label: Genesis 5:3
thread.text: And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:

precepts.label: Genesis 1:26
precepts.why:
“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Why is it written like that? Seth was in Adam's likeness, after Adam's image. It never says that about Cain. John said Cain “was of that wicked one”: Cain was in the image of Satan, not in the image of Adam.

Go back to the beginning: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth”. That was the point. God's image was given to man, and that image carried down to Seth, but everybody is not in God's image.

Everybody came from Adam, yes, but Satan's kids came from Adam too; that was Cain's lineage. Coming from Adam does not make someone a child of God. The image and likeness went through Seth, and that is the line to follow through Genesis.

precepts.label: Genesis 2:7
precepts.why:
“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” That was Adam. God made Adam in his own image and breathed the breath of life into him.

Read Genesis 5:3 again with that in mind: Adam “begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Seth was in the image of Adam, and Adam was in the image of God. So Seth carried God's image.

Cain was not in the image of God. He was not in Adam's image, and he was not in God's image; he was of that wicked one. That is why everybody is not a child of God, and why Cain's line and Seth's line have to be read differently. All of this was playing out in the city Cain built, named Enoch after his son.

thread.label: Genesis 6:1-14
thread.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,

precepts.label: 1 John 3:1
precepts.why:
All of this was happening in the city called Enoch, named after Cain's son. Genesis says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” In Christianity they say the sons of God are angels coming down. John shows who the sons of God are: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”.

The sons of God is not talking about angels. It is talking about men, our people. Before we were called Israelites, we were called the sons of God.

Genesis 6 proves it: “And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh”. God is angry with man, the sons of God, who are flesh, not angels. It is hard to see how Christian scholars can read that and say angels.

So when the sons of God took them wives of all which they chose, it is talking about interracial marriage: we started marrying the women of other nations. It still happens, a brother bringing in a white woman and claiming she is of the tribe of Gad, when everybody knows she is an Edomite.

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Everybody is waiting for our manifestation, for us to be called the sons of God. That is the same name Genesis 6 gives, which settles who the sons of God were: men of our people, not angels.

With that understanding, Genesis 6 reads plainly. It says that “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” That spark from God that we had produced renowned and powerful men on the earth, and they were battling the giants.

But we were not righteous; we had already started breaking God's laws inside that city. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” Think of the great cities today, like New York City: murder, wicked music, buying and selling, stealing. It is the same thing going on now that was going on then, down to a married man looking over at other nations' women.

“The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.” God told Noah, “the earth is filled with violence through them”, and that “them” goes back to Cain's seed. What we read in Genesis 4 about Cain's children affected all people on the earth. So God said, “Make thee an ark of gopher wood”. The sons of God were meant to be manifest, but by mixing with Cain's world they were corrupted with it.

thread.label: Genesis 9:1-16
thread.text: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:29-30
precepts.why:
After the flood, “God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.” Why replenish? Because God killed everybody on the planet. People say God is all love; then they have never read the Bible. He is all love when you obey, but he is also a great and terrible God.

Then: “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things.” This is the first time meat was introduced into our diet. Genesis 1 shows the diet before: “Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.” Our diet was herbs and seeds.

And not only ours: “to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.” Even the lions, the tigers and the bears ate herbs and vegetables. Nobody ate meat until Genesis 9:3. So when someone asks how the animals on the ark did not eat each other, the answer is that their diet was herbs and vegetables. When God introduced meat to us after the flood, the carnivores came with it.

Even then God set a limit: “But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.” Do not eat anything with blood in it. And he gave a sign: “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.” The rainbow was first created there, as a promise that the waters would no more become a flood to destroy all flesh, and it has nothing to do with LGBT.

precepts.label: Isaiah 31:1-2
precepts.why:
The Lord is a man of war, and his vengeance is on all the nations read in Psalms 83; he has a big payback coming for all of them. Egypt is one example. Exodus 15 says “Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea”, and Isaiah 31 shows what all that power was worth: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong”.

Did the power help them? No. All their chariots and all their war materials did not help them at all. And “they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!” We did not look to the Holy One of Israel, to our God, to save us. The God of Israel is the only God that is going to save us out of all this foolishness. The wars are going to come to the point where thermonuclear ICBMs are put in full effect and a lot of people die, and the question to ask yourself is, will it be us?

“Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words”. He is not calling back his word. Evil is set for all these nations, and these nations will be destroyed. Where will you be? You cannot have God to trust in and Christ coming to save you while you sit in confederacy with all these nations, thinking all nations are going to be saved and we are all together. That is not the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

So the right hand that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy” in Exodus 15:6 is the same hand that will overthrow every nation Israel trusts in instead of him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 51:13-14
precepts.why:
Prophecy is coming to pass and there is no stopping it. The wild and crazy ones made demands to the proud one: not only fall back out of our country, but pay us back for all the destruction. The proud man says no, we are not going to do that. Even while they talk about peace talks, God has them in the trick bag.

“O thou that dwellest upon many waters”: that is New Babylon, America. She is “abundant in treasures”: rich from all the nations, because they have taken all the land and all the resources and oppressed all the people. And “thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness.” The Most High is already telling her that her end is come and it is time to step down. She is not going to step down, so God is going to put her down.

“The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself”: the same Lord of hosts who is a man of war in Exodus 15:3. “Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers; and they shall lift up a shout against thee.” Those caterpillars are the wild and crazy ones.

If proud Babylon gives in to the demands, she loses her sovereignty over the economy, and that is her downfall. Because she is prideful and already in power, she will not do it, so it leads to war, and God activates the caterpillars. Either way it goes to war. As the Lord cast Pharaoh's chariots into the sea, he will consume this enemy as stubble.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:5
precepts.why:
Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will “by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.” Exodus 20:5 shows who that is spoken of: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.”

Of them that hate me. To disobey God's commandments is to demonstrate that you hate God. He pardons iniquity and transgression and sin, but if we are guilty of breaking his laws, we are going to pay.

That is why this is read in the wilderness, right after the commandments and statutes were given. A lot of us did not learn from the mistakes we made back then. We came back and did the same damn thing, still wicked and evil and covetous to this day, and the Most High is going to keep sending those afflictions until the lesson is learned. Read the book of your fathers to find out what we did and why all this hell is on us, and you will know what not to do today.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:17
precepts.why:
The iniquity visited upon the children in Exodus 34:7 is the same sin carried from generation to generation, and covetousness is one of them. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.”

To covet means to take what does not belong to you: to take it by wickedness, by deceit. The same BS we were doing back then, we still do today, coveting our neighbour's house and our neighbour's wife.

Then, “nor his ox”: hold it right there. That points to Exodus 22, the same chapter Negroes use to beguile you sisters. The whole of that chapter is about thou shalt not covet. Then, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”: you are not supposed to covet, to take, anything that belongs to that father, that neighbour.

So the iniquity of the fathers that is still being visited on us is the same covetousness, and we should learn not to carry that evil all the way up to now.

precepts.label: Exodus 22:1-17
precepts.why:
Exodus 22 is the law put in place for those that wanted to do evil, and it is proper. The whole chapter is about putting restraints on covetousness. It is not telling you how you are supposed to move. It is like a speeding ticket: your insurance goes way up, and that is the consequence of breaking the original law. Drive the damn speed limit.

“If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.” That is covetousness: you coveted thy neighbour's ox, exactly what Exodus 20:17 forbids. If you do, you pay for the one you stole and give him five oxen for it.

“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” The maid belongs to her father. To entice her means you coveted to get her; you did it behind the father's back, in deceit. You broke the tenth commandment, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” You lured her away from her father, and you are going to try to tell me that is righteous? You are a damn fool. And a woman that has no wisdom will follow that and pay for the judgment.

Verse 17 kills it: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” The father said hell no. Even though you enticed her, you are not taking her. That is what happened with Dinah: she was enticed, spoken to sweetly and kindly; she was not raped. Even though he wanted to marry her, her brothers said no, snatched her out of that house, and she had to sit there defiled.

That should be a warning to you women. No backdoor marriages will be approved, period. If we have to snatch you out, and you have to sit with that scarlet letter knowing you were defiled, that is better than being tied up with somebody that means you pure evil. How could you even respect a man who went behind your father's back, your protection's back? This is the guilty that Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will by no means clear.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:43-47
precepts.why:
Balaam, in his trance, saw that Israel’s “king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” Agag was an Edomite, a real tall one. The kingdom that is going to be exalted is the kingdom of the Lord, and the king higher than Agag is Christ.

Ezra saw that same king: “in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted”. Ezra asked the angel who these were, and he answered, “These be they that have put off the mortal clothing, and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned, and receive palms.” Then, “What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands?” And the answer: “It is the Son of God”.

So that is what Balaam saw in the spirit realm about the Israelites. His king shall be taller even than Agag. There will be no question in the kingdom which one is the Son of God. He is going to be the tallest one, and not by an inch or a foot; it is going to be astronomically clear. You will look and say, that is the Son of God right there.

And Balaam saw more of him: “he shall eat up the nations his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows.” Balaam saw Christ destroying the nations. And “Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee”: anybody that blesses Israel shall be blessed, and anybody that curses us shall be cursed.

precepts.label: Joshua 13:22
precepts.why:
Balaam dealt with enchantments, which lets us know he was a witch, a soothsayer, a diviner. When it says “the spirit of God came upon him”, notice the little s: this is on the left hand side. It is not the Holy Spirit coming on Balaam. He would fall into trances with his eyes wide open and see visions, and he knew it was the Lord sending that spirit upon him, which is why he told Balak he could not go beyond the commandment of the Lord. Even so, he saw Christ only from afar: “I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh”, because he is not an Israelite.

What happened to Balaam? “Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.” What was he? The soothsayer: a witch, a warlock.

The Lord had used that witch, sending unrighteous angels to tell him this and tell him that. Then he told the Israelites: kill Balaam, destroy him; he is not our people. God got tired of him and had him put to death.

That is the end of the false prophet. Balaam could see all the way to the latter days and speak blessings over Israel, but his gift came from the left hand side, and he was slain among the enemies of Israel.

thread.label: Numbers 30:6-8
thread.text: And if she had at all an husband, when she vowed, or uttered ought out of her lips, wherewith she bound her soul;

precepts.label: Numbers 30:3-5
precepts.why:
Numbers 30:6-8 is about your prayers, sisters, and the power the Most High gave the husband over the wife. If the husband hears her vow and holds his peace, “then her vows shall stand”; but if he disallows her the day he hears it, “he shall make her vow which she vowed, and that which she uttered with her lips, wherewith she bound her soul, of none effect: and the Lord shall forgive her.” Some of you will go to the Most High praying against your husband, and he can say, Lord, do not listen to that trash.

Keep reading back in the chapter and it speaks of the father, for those of you who do not have a husband. It starts with the man: “If a man vow a vow unto the Lord, or swear an oath to bind his soul with a bond; he shall not break his word”.

Then: “If a woman also vow a vow unto the Lord, and bind herself by a bond, being in her father’s house in her youth”. Being where? In her father’s house. “And her father hear her vow, and her bond wherewith she hath bound her soul, and her father shall hold his peace at her: then all her vows shall stand”.

“But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth; not any of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her.”

So God also gave the father power over the daughter. The same power the husband has over the wife’s vow, the father has over his daughter’s vow while she is in his house. That is the order the Most High set, and nobody made it up: do not get mad at us, we are reading the Bible.

precepts.label: Joshua 2:15-16
precepts.why:
When the king of Jericho sent for the men, Rahab hid them “with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof”, and sent the pursuers the wrong way. Then she went further: “Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall.” “And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.”

She not only helped the prophets, she helped them with an exit. She gave them a way out and a plan: where to go, how long to hide, and when it would be safe to go their way.

These examples are in here for our learning. In these last days some brothers and sisters are going to be looked to to hide the prophets. As we build this spiritual underground railroad, some of y'all will be required to help one another, and sometimes when you help brothers and sisters you are going to put yourself in danger.

Is that you, sister? Is that you, brother? Are you ready to do that for your nation? Or are you going to sell out to keep this body that gets a headache, gets diarrhea, gets belly aches, coughing and all kind of infirmities? The scriptures tell you we have to be ready in these last days.

That is why Hebrews 13 follows it: “Let brotherly love continue.” “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.” Start small, in your household. Make that guest room ready to receive a guest; if you can't afford an extra room, instead of buying that leather couch, get a pullout couch. If a prophet is on the run and you can provide shelter for two days, a meal and shelter for a prophet, that is a blessing for you. That is the mindset of Rahab, and the mindset we have to have in these last days.

precepts.label: Psalms 10:17
precepts.why:
“For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.” What is the heart? The mind. Ezra had prepared his mind to seek the Lord his God. We are in captivity, always working and tired; some days you get stressed. But the Most High has to remind us that we are living in the last days. So brothers, prepare your minds; sisters, prepare your minds.

David shows who the Lord prepares: “Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the humble: thou wilt prepare their heart, thou wilt cause thine ear to hear”. We are the humble. We are supposed to humble ourselves to whatever the Bible says we ought to do.

And when we humble ourselves, the Lord hears our desire and prepares our hearts. We will prepare our minds. That is what Ezra did before he went to teach Israel, and that is what is required of us now, as we watch Iran and Israel go to war and America get involved, and more of our people wake up and repent.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:17
precepts.why:
Why prepare our minds and our spirits? Because war is imminent. We are seeing Iran and Israel at war and America getting involved, and the wars are only going to get worse. What we see right now is a birthing pain. Yet all of us are supposed to rejoice, because the scriptures already told us this was going to happen.

Sirach says: “They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight”. All of us that fear the Lord will prepare our minds, so that whatever evil comes upon the earth, we will remain faithful in serving the Lord.

That is Ezra's example: a heart prepared, and a soul humbled in the Lord's sight, ready to seek the law, do it, and teach it, whatever comes.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:3-4
precepts.why:
Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law and to teach it. Sirach shows why: “A man of understanding trusteth in the law; and the law is faithful unto him, as an oracle.” We must trust in the laws of God, and the law will be faithful unto us.

“Prepare what to say, and so thou shalt be heard”. We have to prepare what to say. Prepare what to say in prayer when we speak to the Most High, and we will be heard. Prepare what to say and teach in the streets, and we will be heard. We must prepare to lead, guide and organize blacks and Hispanics.

“and bind up instruction, and then make answer.” Bind up the instruction first, and then make answer. That is how Ezra could teach in Israel statutes and judgments: he had prepared his heart before he opened his mouth.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:17
precepts.why:
This is to the brothers who teach, the up-and-coming soldiers in the MOV program. Ezra prepared his heart to teach in Israel, and the Lord says: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.”

Who is speaking? The Most High said, I have made thee a watchman. It is not the Bishop that made you a watchman. It is not the deacons, and it is not the captains. The Lord called you to be a watchman. That is why you were called into this truth: to warn our people, to warn Israel that they need to repent.

Habakkuk shows the watchman's posture: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower”. He is awake and paying attention. As watchmen we must be faithful and pay attention to the signs of the times, hear the word at the Lord's mouth, and give Israel warning from him.

His seed built the city Enoch: tents and cattle, buying and selling with unrighteous pricing; the harp and organ, and not holy music; Tubal-cain and every artificer in brass and iron, weapons; Lamech avenged seventy and sevenfold, wiping out a whole line. The sons of God took wives of all which they chose, the earth was filled with violence, and God destroyed it.

Think about the great cities today, like New York City: murder, wicked music, buying and selling, stealing, the wife looking over at the white woman or the Chinese woman. The same thing going on now is what was going on back then, because man is what he was.

Sirach shows the way: “If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.”

This is the brother in the world trying to repent, trying to get his house in order and straighten it out, while his wife keeps up the traps of Ecclesiastes 7:26: her heart snares and nets, her hands as bands, creating chaos and assignments so he can't get to camp, to the brothers, to the meetings. She doesn't want to listen. Then let her go. And it goes both ways; it is about you men too.

But understand: this is not talking about a biblical marriage. Once you get married in this truth, she is yours for life, unless she commits adultery. There is no divorce in the Bible, and we don't dissolve marriages up in here; it is written in our rules. This is for those coming in from outside this truth, with all kinds of situations.

So the man who pleases God escapes from her. But if you allow yourself to be destroyed, you were indeed wicked, and the woman sent to you was your portion for real.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:15
precepts.why:
Paul speaks to the same case: “But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.”

The man was wicked and inherited a wicked woman. Why? God orchestrated it, to see whether he would stay there, and to reflect what is in us so that we can change. The Lord is interested in the elect, so he puts us through trials and temptations to see if we will overcome them.

The bondage is the worldly marriage. When the spouse says, I don't care what you do, I want nothing to do with that Bible, and makes it plain and won't bend, still cooking pork and ham hocks on one side of the stove, this half is for you since you're keeping those laws, we're going to keep eating chitlins and hog maws, the house smelling like butt: if the unbelieving depart, let them depart. That is the woman of Ecclesiastes 7:26 whose heart is traps and nets, and whoso pleases God shall escape.

But those coming out of these situations have a lot of work to do before they can even think about properly marrying, and brothers and sisters are impatient. Leadership are the fathers of the men and women, and we have the records. When we tell you to lean back and let the brother or sister work on themselves, it is for a good reason, because the backdoor marriage stories are horrible, and they get worse every time a new one pops up.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:1-4
precepts.why:
Before anyone walks away, look at the other side. At a Passover panel years ago a sister asked when she could walk away from her husband in the world. They had been together about ten years, through Africanism, through Islam, through different things. In his mind this truth might be just another fad. Wait, sister. Lean back.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” He is worldly, but he isn't telling you to break the laws of God, so still deal with him properly. Chaste means with discipline: you aren't cursing him out. He watches the change in you, sees the fear of the Lord in you, and sees it is serious, not a phase.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, “the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.” She puts on proper clothing, and tells him: my husband, I want you to come in and take command, so I can deal with you as a proper wife. He comes home from catching hell at work and she knows how to pull him out of it, and he asks, where are you learning this wisdom? If he is righteous, he comes in behind you; we have seen it many times.

Men do the same: a brother who was in sin with his wife last week wants to turn the house upside down this week. Give her a chance to see you're serious. Wives have said, I didn't know he was this serious; he was willing to let me go, and they came in behind him. That is the Most High giving righteousness to righteousness.

“Shake the hand”: warn our people, “that they may go into the gates of the nobles.” The nations have drunk Babylon's wine, her lies and philosophies, what Daniel calls her policy, and therefore the nations are mad. War is coming, and in the midst of all that war, the prophets are still crying aloud, showing our people their transgression so they can be saved.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 5:11

Isaiah sees the war coming on Babylon and the prophets still lifting up the banner and exalting the voice. Paul says why we do it: “Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men.” In Job he is called the king of terrors. We know what the Lord is going to do. The Lord set us up as watchmen, and since we know the terror of the Lord, we must persuade men.

“But we are made manifest unto God; and I trust also are made manifest in your consciences.”

Who are we trying to persuade? Our people, in the midst of all kinds of sin. So brothers, we must be studying, so that when we come across our people we are able to help them. The scripture says the whole head is sick: we are sick individuals ourselves. But we must learn to discipline ourselves, and we must learn how to persuade our people to change their lives.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:9-10
precepts.why:
These are the kind of people we are trying to persuade to change: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane.” It is for our people who are lawless.

But there is repentance for those spirits. These are the spirits we are trying to win over and get to submit to the Lord.

“For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”: women with all kinds of men, men with all kinds of women, and homosexuality. There is repentance for all of these sins. Some of us are struggling with one, two, three, four, five of these. God damn. We have demons on us.

The only way to get it out is to have one counsellor of a thousand and open up. That is the problem: some of you don't want to open up, and by the time we find out what you are struggling with, it's too late to help. It doesn't mean you can't repent, but it is a lot harder because you kept it secret so long, and by the time you tell us you are already having sex and we have to throw you out. “For menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.” How many of us lie? We all lie. Why didn't you come to the Sabbath? Can you persuade a murderer, a lesbian, a homosexual to change their life? Can you turn a liar or a thief into a soldier? You can, and the proof is that you are sitting in the building. Don't say only Deacon Eythan or Black Rhino knows how to talk to people.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:8
precepts.why:
Habakkuk was in the Babylonian captivity, around 606 BC. The princes and the king were taken away, and Habakkuk was left because he was a poor prophet, so he stood on his tower complaining about what ancient Babylon did to us under Nebuchadnezzar. The Lord answered, “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah explains the tables for new people: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

The table is the book, and the book is what we call the Bible today. The vision was not only for Habakkuk's day; it was noted in a book “for the time to come”, because “the vision is yet for an appointed time”.

Sometimes you read prophecy and want it to happen in your lifetime, but God says it is for a later date: though it tarry, wait for it. It was written down in the book so that when the end came it would speak and not lie. We are in that time period now, and the vision is plain on the tables for whoever will read it.

precepts.label: Amos 8:11-12
precepts.why:
The vision is written plain “that he may run that readeth it.” Amos explains the running: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord”.

There would be a famine of the word of the Lord. “And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east, they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.” People would travel from sea to sea, running to and fro, looking for the word and not finding it.

That is what happened after Christ and the disciples died: there was no truth being taught in the earth, nowhere. By the time of Constantine, around 325 AD, you had the churches, and there was no truth there; they were worshiping idols. Some of the Moors were Islamic, and some were black Jews following the Talmud and the Cabala. When white folks rose up it went crazy, into idolatry like you never saw: the church fathers making doctrine, and Tertullian, the devil that created the Trinity.

And they were traveling. The crusades went here and there trying to get the cup Christ drank from and to find the cross, trying to get some kind of glimpse of understanding. They ran to and fro, just as Amos said, because the word written plain in the book had nobody left to teach it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 7:28-30
precepts.why:
Amos says they would run to and fro to seek the word of the Lord and not find it. Ezra gives the precept that explains why: “For my son Jesus shall be revealed with those that be with him, and they that remain shall rejoice within four hundred years.” Those with him were the apostles, the followers, the disciples. From Ezra's time to the time of Christ was four hundred years.

“After these years shall my son Christ die, and all men that have life.” Christ was crucified, and all the apostles and all the disciples that followed him either died or were murdered and crucified by Rome. All the men and women that had understanding were dead.

“And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.” So that no man that has truth shall remain. From the time after Christ and the disciples died, there was no truth being taught anywhere in the earth. There were no Israelites saying, we are the Israelites and we have to keep the commandments. Instead you had the church fathers, the damn devils, making doctrine, and Tertullian creating the Trinity.

That silence is the famine of hearing the words of the Lord. The world ran to and fro in it for centuries, and that is why the vision had to wait for its appointed time: at the end it shall speak, and not lie.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 1:6
precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. Who is he talking about? Go back to chapter 1: “For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs.”

Did not America do that? The white man came throughout this land and took all the dwelling places that were not his. And the so-called Israelis are doing the same thing over there today.

Though Habakkuk prophesied in the days of Babylon, the vision was for the appointed time at the end, and we are in that time now. So the proud man of chapter 2 is the man raised up in the last days. “He transgresseth by wine”: philosophies and lies. “He is a proud man”, like Edom in Obadiah. He “neither keepeth at home”: America is in everybody's country, with over 850 bases worldwide. He “enlargeth his desire as hell”: when he takes your land he brings democracy and Christianity, and your whole society turns to hell. He destabilizes and bombs your country, then lets a remnant come to the United States, which is why America is called the great melting pot.

“Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his!” Did you forget Venezuela already? He took Venezuela and the oil. He steals and robs, possessing dwelling places that are not his, just as the Chaldeans did.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:13-14
precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evil!” Is that not what Nimrod and them were doing? Before we get scattered, let us build a tower and get up to heaven. Today's Babylon has the same characteristics and attributes. Jeremiah said it too: “Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from me shall spoilers come unto her”.

Isaiah shows the heart of it: “For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”. That is space travel. NASA and SpaceX are advancing plans for a permanent presence on the moon through the Artemis program, and Artemis 2 just went up. Elon Musk talks of colonizing Mars. Why does Esau the Edomite want to go to Mars? Because it is the red planet.

“I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: that is us, in North America. “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: that is airplanes. How could that part be true, because you see it, while the verse above it about the stars is fake? You can have your doubting Thomas saying it's all fake. Is it fake like the planes you fly on and the helicopters you see? Stop watching stupid YouTube clips.

He sets his nest on high thinking he will be delivered from the power of evil when destruction comes. But he “hast consulted shame to thy house by cutting off many people”. “Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and stablisheth a city by iniquity!” America was built with blood: the schools, the churches and the courthouses are on the bones and blood of our brothers and sisters. Did not Cain establish a city by iniquity? There is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.why:
“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” The Lord puts the unity of brethren first. Then the love of neighbours: the charity, the long-suffering.

This is what the gathering of Zephaniah 2:1 has to look like. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: the nation hated upon the earth has to come together in the last days. But as we gather, we have to fix our character flaws, show ourselves friendly, and endeavor to keep the unity, and endeavor is an enduring word, not one to be taken lightly.

Unity of brethren does not mean you cannot correct one another or admonish one another. It means you expect highly of each other. We need correction, admonishment, counsel and advice amongst each other. Those who push you toward hard things, who tell you the harsh truth when a lie would be easier, are your people. That is how the gathered nation stands up beautiful before God and men.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:17
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” Love for one another means we are not supposed to suffer sin on one another.

So if I see my brother or my sister in the midst of sin, I might have to give them that rough talk. And it is to do what? To put them back in the righteous mindset. Real admonishment and love, being able to correct your brothers, comes with a little bit of hard criticism. You cannot take it emotionally, and you cannot take it personally. Tell the brother he is fat: fix it, brother. That is love, not hate.

Friends who roast each other are the loyal ones; those who value your success over the need to be liked are the ones who truly want your best. Their words are heavy, but their loyalty is pure. Don’t think that because a man is charitable he doesn’t correct anybody. We have to stop thinking with that emotional Christianity.

This is how the nation of Zephaniah 2:1 gathers. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: in the last days we gather with the believers who fear the Lord, and until we receive our homeland we are all we got. Rebuking one another in love keeps the gathered body clean and keeps the unity.

If you start from Genesis, you find out that salvation and rulership of the earth is only for the Israelites through Christ. The Bereans show how it is done: “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

The honour of kings is to search it out: to find who Moab, Ammon, Gad and Asia are today. The matter is concealed, but it is there for those who search.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 1:7
precepts.why:
“Now it is high time to awake out of sleep”. We see all these things going on and some of y’all still stay asleep, not even paying attention to what is going on in the earth. Y’all crazy as hell. You need to prepare ye war, and the first place to prepare is the mind: guard your mind from fear.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” God gave you power, love and a sound mind. Some of y’all are scared. Christ told them to sell their garment and buy a sword, and some are still scared to buy one. Christ said do it.

There is a time and place for everything under the sun, and that time is going to come. So prepare mentally. We are a nonviolent people; all we want to do is serve the Lord. But we will protect and defend ourselves.

Waking out of sleep means not letting fear keep you from doing what Christ commanded. “Now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”, and a mind given power, love and soundness by God is ready for what is coming.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:8
precepts.why:
Waking out of sleep means staying awake: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

You have to stay sober and vigilant, because the enemy looks for open doors and distracted people. As soon as one of y’all gets distracted from the mission, they are coming. That is why every time somebody leaves, we see who shows up: the damn Christian apologists.

They take you all the way back into the world and have you speaking all manner of evil, but they are not telling you to prepare yourself mentally for what is to come. They are just trying to destroy what we are doing. They are not trying to save your soul. They say they are already saved; they are not saved from the nuclear missiles that are about to drop.

So the one who is asleep is the one the roaring lion devours. It is high time to wake up, stay sober, stay vigilant and stay on the mission, because the adversary is walking about looking for whoever drifts.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:4-5
precepts.why:
“Take heed that no man deceive you.” Prepare ye war: you have to prepare yourself mentally, and part of that is not letting any man deceive you. Do not let deception take you.

“For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.” He is telling you that many false prophets and many false Christs are going to rise. And it is happening: there are men online right now literally saying that they are Jesus. Freaking Jesus. Freak ass dude.

Christ said more in the same chapter: “For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets”. That is going to happen, and those who are spiritually asleep will be the ones deceived.

So awaking out of sleep is guarding your mind from deception. The time is late, our salvation is nearer than when we believed, and the deceivers are already here. Take heed.

precepts.label: Psalms 136:8-17
precepts.why:
Paul says God “will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. There is no temptation that should derail us from inheriting the wide place, the kingdom that sits within the narrow passage (2 Esdras 7), because God's mercies endure for ever. David shows that mercy: “The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.” The Lord declared the end from the beginning and created all of this. We acknowledge his greatness and his mercy, and we tap into that comfort under the shadow of his wings.

“To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endureth for ever: And brought out Israel from among them”. The Most High killed our enemies for us because he had mercy on us. We cried in Egypt, the Lord heard our cries and said, go down, Moses, tell Pharaoh to let my people go, or I will kill his firstborn.

“With a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm”, “To him which divided the Red sea into parts”, “And made Israel to pass through the midst of it”, “But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea”, “To him which led his people through the wilderness”, “To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever”.

We saw all of this, and we still get here today and do evil, just as our fathers under the cloud did. The Most High is trying to set us back up, but he wants to make sure we are in the right spiritual posture to inherit the kingdom. He lets us use his Bible as spiritual weapons to fight off the evil temptations so we can get to the wide.

precepts.label: Lamentations 3:20-24
precepts.why:
Paul says the things that happened to our fathers “are written for our admonition”. Jeremiah shows how we hold on to them: “My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.” The them is the afflictions and punishments we are supposed to remember for breaking God's commandments in the past, and we are humbled because of it.

“This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Do you hear that? That is the love the Lord has for us, his mercy enduring for ever. He loves you, sisters; he loves you, brothers. His compassions and his mercies fail not.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” His mercies are renewed every day, forgiving us. We say the Lord's prayer, we ask the Lord for mercy and to forgive our transgressions, and he does it. And we are still playing with sin.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” So now we are in the posture where he has given us a way to escape the evil all around us.

precepts.label: Psalms 23:5
precepts.why:
God will with the temptation “make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” While we endure the encounters of temptation that are common to us all, even the temptations of our own lusts, the Lord prepares a table for us: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.” Why? Because his mercies endure for ever.

The table is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah shows it: “write it before them in a table, and note it in a book”. The tables are what we are supposed to be reading.

But we read the tables and talk about what's going on overseas while our own spirit is rotten. We read it like entertainment instead of changing what is really going on in us.

Brothers and sisters, you are in the greatest place on the planet earth, and some of you don't even realize it. You are getting teaching that tells you what is happening in the future, because we know the future from reading the Bible. And some of you play games, scorn what is brought out, and take this for a joke. The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies; eat from it.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:2
precepts.why:
The table the Lord prepares before us in the presence of our enemies is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

The Lord told the prophet Habakkuk: since you want to get out of captivity, write the vision down, and make it plain upon the tables. That is what we are supposed to be reading.

Make it plain “that he may run that readeth it”: when we bring this out, everybody is going to be running, and we are going to run to teach it. The Bible is going to turn this whole system upside down: these are they which have turned the world upside down. But we have to be in it like that, not reading about overseas like entertainment while our own spirit is rotten.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:8
precepts.why:
Paul says what happened to our fathers is “written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” Isaiah shows why it was written: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

This is to the wicked Israelites, us, our people. Go write it before them in a table, and put a note in the book about their wickedness, our wickedness, “that it may be for the time to come”: for today.

And it goes on: “That this is a rebellious people”. That is what is going on with our people; our people are rebellious. But the Bible is here to correct you and straighten you out. If you want it, there is a way for you to get it.

Those who refuse to learn from the past by reading it are doomed to repeat it. You will repeat it because you refuse to learn, and the same spirits will follow you and attach themselves to you, the way people move to a new town, a new job or a new congregation and the same problem follows. The Lord sends those spirits as a mirror to show you what is wrong in you. Learn it from the book, and you won't have to learn it again.

thread.label: 1 Corinthians 10:14
thread.text: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.

precepts.label: Exodus 20:3-5
precepts.why:
“Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry”. That is in the New Testament, for you black Christians, you black apologists, you black pastors who say the law is done away with. Why would Paul write it if the law was done away? Because it goes right back to Exodus 20: “Thou shalt have no other gods before me”.

“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”. That is where 1 Corinthians 10:14 comes from.

Valentine's Day is idolatry; its origin is Februus and Lupercalia, a fertility rite in which women presented themselves to be struck because it was believed to help with fertility. When you sit up there and celebrate Valentine's Day, you are putting Februus, whoever the hell that is, and Lupercalia before the Lord. What's wrong with Christmas? It's idolatry. Your birthday? Idolatry. Halloween? Idolatry. That's what's wrong with it.

The Lord gave us our own high holy days, in Leviticus 23. The Destruction of Nicanor began last night at sundown, the victory recorded in 1 Maccabees 7 and 2 Maccabees 14 and 15, when Judas Maccabeus defeated and killed Nicanor, the Seleucid Syrian Greek commander who came to crush Israel and threaten the temple. Tonight at sundown begins Purim, when we were saved from being wiped out in the Persian Empire: the enemy was Haman, and the deliverance came through Esther and Mordecai. Our enemies' holidays, the Fourth of July and Christmas, are victories over us. Ours are victories over our enemies. Flee from their idolatry and keep what the Lord gave us.

precepts.label: Psalms 85:11
precepts.why:
“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. You are at war right now in your spirit, with evil temptations pushed on every front: family members, school, work, even your own thoughts as you sit here. The weapons are not guns; the weapons are the commandments of God, and they are mighty.

Mighty to pull down what? Lies. That is what the Bible does; that is how we tear the lies down. We open up the Bible and swallow up the lies, like it says in the Psalms: “Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven.” We open this Bible, and the lies are swallowed up.

So “Casting down imaginations” is casting down lies, “and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”, and the knowledge of God is the law, the Bible. When you open this Bible and apply the commandments, you get rid of those impulsive, sinful thoughts and bring every thought “into captivity” under the obedience of Christ. That is how you walk straight past your temptation.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 8:11
precepts.why:
The weapons of our warfare are the commandments. You are supposed to answer your impulses, your sinful temptations, with the commandments of God, and that is supposed to turn you from the door of temptation. If you understood that death is around the corner, you would listen to these laws.

But the wicked man thinks judgment is far off: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” Because the judgment is not immediate, his sick, evil mind is emboldened to commit evil and sin, and he leaves the commandments to the side. You had better recognize where you are.

That is the war inside you. The Lord isn't asking you to pick up a gun and go do something out there; he is asking you to get your mind right and set this mark in your head to change your behavior. We don't advocate anyone initiating aggression; if someone comes at you with a rope or a knife, you defend yourself. But the gung-ho brothers who can't wait for war can't even discipline their food. The war to win first is against the heart that sin makes bold.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:13
precepts.why:
“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” Some of our people can't wait: they want to be part of the war in the streets, casting out demons, getting their names on the Saturday night specials: brother, get a good angle of me, I want my video to go up Saturday. But here's the stipulation: when your obedience is fulfilled. That means there is no impediment left in your spirit to commit sin; you are walking straight in your spirit, your household, with your children, blameless. Then you can go out and correct your people.

That is what the Apocrypha says: “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. First set your house in order. Your physical house can't be set in order if your spiritual house, meaning your damn head, is not in order. You haven't even checked your own wicked thoughts, your own actions, your own temptations, and you are trying to correct your wife, your son and your daughter.

Set your head in order; then you can set your house in order; then you can reprove your people. That is when your obedience is fulfilled, and you can revenge all disobedience, because you checked it first within yourself. We want to play warrior, to look good, while there are demons all up in us that we have not corrected yet.

Paul says “that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith”, and he ends by saying meats were created “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” What is the truth they depart from? David says: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

God's law is the truth, and that is what these religions would have you depart from. We are in the latter times now. Some of you men and women listening will depart from the truth of Christ: some because of persecution for the word's sake, and some because you see signs and wonders, technological signs and wonders, and believe we have been wrong all this time. It is already written, as Christ said: “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders”, and “Behold, I have told you before.”

They give heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: they have the Bible, but they are hypocrites. If Christ is our commander, what does that make us? Soldiers. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” And a soldier cannot live for this world: “For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ.”

We are at war. Spiritual war. We don’t use guns or weapons or any of that stuff, but we are at spiritual war, and spiritual war is the most powerful mode of warfare. Our forefathers understood that in this gospel, this mission we are on, we are all soldiers on the battlefield. That is how Paul referred to his fellow laborers.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” In order to please God, who has called us to be soldiers, we cannot be entangled with the affairs of this life. If you are entangled with the affairs of this life, that means you want to please men. We can’t move like that. Our conversation is in heaven, and we are looking for the Saviour to come from there.

So what does God want us to do? What does God require of us? What is God’s mission? Gather the twelve tribes of Israel from the four corners of the earth. Let the elect be sealed; let the 144 be sealed, so we can go home. That is the business of a good soldier of Jesus Christ, with the mind of a judge that comes from biblical education, instead of the affairs of this life.

precepts.why:
Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 9:26-28
precepts.why:
“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:12
precepts.why:
Solomon’s ships “came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold”. Isaiah uses that same gold: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

We often read this and keep going, and some will say it is the best gold, but we don’t go deeper into what the gold of Ophir is. The gold of Ophir is an exceptionally fine, pure gold, prized in the ancient world, famous as what King Solomon and King Hiram of Tyre brought in, and its exact location remains one of history’s greatest archaeological mysteries.

That is what the Most High is going to make you men: that pure fine gold. The same tribes who crossed the waters on those old maritime routes, whose record the historians call mythical, are the men the Most High will make more precious than the golden wedge of Ophir.
